INFORMATIONS.PHASE_NUMBER_TOOLTIP: Single-phase meters handle up to ~7 kVA; three-phase meters are used for higher-power installations. Affects DSO billing thresholds.
INFORMATIONS.READING_FREQUENCY_TOOLTIP: How often the DSO reads the physical meter. Monthly reading provides finer billing granularity; annual reading means interim months are estimated from consumption profiles.
INFORMATIONS.TARIF_GROUP_TOOLTIP: Voltage level at which the meter is connected to the grid. Low voltage = standard residential/commercial connection. High voltage = industrial or large-scale connection. Set by your DSO.
INFORMATIONS.WITHDRAWAL_POWER_TOOLTIP: Maximum power (in kVA) the meter is contractually allowed to draw from the grid at any instant. Found on the network contract.
INFORMATIONS.TOTAL_GENERATING_CAPACITY_TOOLTIP: Maximum power (in kVA) that the production installation connected to this meter can inject into the grid.
INFORMATIONS.AMPERAGE_TOOLTIP: Current rating of the meter's main circuit breaker in amperes. Used for tariff classification by the DSO.
INFORMATIONS.PRODUCTION_CHAIN_TOOLTIP: Type of renewable or low-carbon installation connected to this meter. Choose "None" if this is a consumption-only meter.
INFORMATIONS.INJECTION_STATUS_TOOLTIP: Describes the meter's relationship to a production installation and who holds the injection rights: owner of the installation, holder of a right-of-use, or none.
INFORMATIONS.GRD_TOOLTIP: Distribution System Operator: the regulated utility company that owns and manages the electricity grid in your area (e.g., Ores, Fluvius, Sibelga).
INFORMATIONS.RATE_TOOLTIP: Single-rate: one price 24/7. Dual-hourly: day and night prices differ. Exclusive night: all energy is billed at the night rate (typically used with large storage or heating systems).
INFORMATIONS.USAGE_TOOLTIP: Residential: private household. Professional: SME or office. Industrial: large industrial site with high-voltage connection or process loads. Determines which DSO tariff schedule applies.
